records.title: Scrimshaw6
observations: Thick red, black and yellow lines crowd a large head on a green ground.
A purple ring and orange loops frame differently drawn eyes.
Two rows of yellow and blue oval marks fill a dark rectangular mouth.
records.reading: A large head nearly fills the square, assembled from thick red, black and yellow lines. Its eyes receive different frames: a purple ring on one side and orange loops on the other. Yellow and blue ovals organize the dark mouth into repeated rows. Those regular marks briefly steady an otherwise crowded surface, allowing the face to emerge without becoming symmetrical.

records.title: Scrimshaw 33
observations: Two large head-like shapes in profile sit side by side against a near-black background, both oriented toward the right, outlined in pale pink and lavender lines that trace jaw, crown, and chin edges.
Dense interior layers of purple, teal, yellow, red, and coral loops fill both forms, with repeated circular scribbles clustered where eye sockets and mouths would sit.
A coral-pink form projects from the left head into the gap between the two figures, its smooth curves contrasting with the tangled lines packed inside each shape.
records.reading: Two hollow-looking heads face the same direction, packed with overlapping color tangles that make their interiors feel restless and crowded. The coral projection from the left head—readable as a nose or jaw—reaches into the dark gap but does not bridge the two forms, leaving each figure isolated despite their closeness. The left head tilts slightly upward while the right juts forward and down, lending the pair an uneven, processional quality.

records.title: Scrimshaw 18
observations: A large head-like form fills the center, built from overlapping rectangular and rounded shapes in red, blue, pink, and cyan against a flat orange background.
Two asymmetric eye-like openings sit mid-face—the left filled with dark crosshatching under pink, the right outlined in cyan and blue with a rounded spiral center.
Loose purple, yellow, and magenta loops orbit the head, extending past its edges into the orange field, creating a tangled halo of looping lines.
records.reading: The head reads as a mask or container: rigid rectangular scaffolding in red and blue holds soft pink fills and dark voids. Zigzag lines across the forehead and teeth-like marks along the lower opening give the form a grinning, almost mechanical quality. The orbiting purple and yellow loops feel restless, as though the figure vibrates against its own outline. Here color blocks and line compete for the same space, producing a sense of pressure inside the frame.

records.title: Scrimshaw8
observations: A long face and narrow neck stand against purple.
White loops mark the eyes and mouth among dark and olive lines.
An additional small oval sits on the forehead beneath a broad yellow loop.
records.reading: A long face extends into a narrow neck against a purple field. White loops pick out the eyes and mouth, while darker strands repeatedly cross their outlines. An additional oval on the forehead and the yellow loop above it complicate the usual facial arrangement. Attention can travel upward through these repetitions, leaving the expression open rather than fixing on the mouth alone.

records.title: Scrimshaw13
observations: A single frontal face fills the frame, topped by a wide dark oval shape built from looping black and teal lines that extends beyond the head's width.
Two large circular eye forms contain tight spiraling marks in red, purple, and black; the left eye sits slightly lower than the right.
A wide red-outlined mouth shape near the center shows jagged white zigzag marks suggesting teeth, with a smaller teal-and-red circle below at the chin.
records.reading: The face stares outward through mismatched spiral eyes, one tighter and darker, the other looser and more flushed with red. A pale yellow-green wash behind the figure lets the tangled purple, red, and black lines read as both structure and agitation. The open mouth with its crude teeth can feel like a shout or a grin—the ambiguity holds. Below the chin, a small secondary circle echoes the eyes, pulling attention downward as if the face is still accumulating.

records.title: Scrimshaw 21
observations: A large tilted head stands on an open yellow ground.
Angular multicolored strokes cross the eyes, nose and toothy mouth.
Long black and colored marks fan outward above the head.
records.reading: A tilted head is built from angular, overlapping marks on a bright yellow ground. The eyes, nose and toothy mouth remain readable even as their contours multiply. Above them, long strokes fan outward and carry the face's restless energy into the surrounding space. The image holds exuberance and strain together rather than settling into a single expression.

records.title: Scrimshaw 40
observations: A thick white X sits over the right side of the face, crossing olive-green and teal lines that fill that area.
A red oval mouth near the bottom center holds jagged yellow-green tooth-like marks, outlined by a bright pink lip shape.
Lime-green and yellow hatched lines spray outward from the top of the head, layered over purple lines that loosely frame the skull shape.
records.reading: Heavy black lines carve a nose bridge and brow, but color escapes everywhere—cyan curls at the throat, magenta along the jaw, yellow above the crown. The white X over one eye area can read as a cancellation or a wound. The open red mouth, with its crude teeth, holds something between a shout and a grin, leaving the mood unresolved. A flat gray field isolates the figure starkly.

records.title: Scrimshaw1
observations: A heavy blue line traces a large head-like shape with zigzag teeth at the bottom, scribbled oval hollows near the center, and sharp angular strokes across the top.
Soft translucent circles in lavender and pale yellow overlap across the background, forming a pastel field that sits behind the sharp blue foreground marks.
Thinner lines in gray, red, pink, and yellow thread through the interior of the blue outline, adding tangled density without overriding the dominant contour.
records.reading: A single heavy blue line carves out a face-like form that reads as both mask and open mouth—zigzag teeth gape, scribbled hollows stare. The soft lavender and yellow circles behind it feel almost gentle, which makes the jagged foreground more unsettling by contrast. Thin colored threads inside the outline suggest a restless interior, as though the shape is barely holding itself together.

records.title: Scrimshaw 41
observations: A large head-like form fills the frame, built from dense overlapping black scribble lines over warm olive-gold and brown washes against a black background.
Three concentric spiral circles sit where eyes and a third upper socket would be, drawn in white and light blue lines, each ringed by black loops.
A wide rectangular mouth shape at the bottom shows a row of white zigzag teeth above a red-orange horizontal bar, framed by scratchy black outlines.
records.reading: The head looms forward, its three hollow spiral sockets staring outward with unsettling symmetry. Tangled black lines pile up like wire, trapping flashes of cyan, pink, yellow, and purple underneath. The jagged white teeth read as a frozen grin or grimace—the expression stays unresolved. Warm golden tones seep through the scribble, giving the dark mass a faint glow that can feel either menacing or mournful depending on where you look.

records.title: Wobbler
observations: Three eye-like forms occupy the head: a small tilted diamond high on the forehead, a broad blue oval below left and a rounded blue frame below right.
A dark horizontal mouth is crossed by closely spaced black vertical bars and white tooth-like marks, above a small outlined chin form.
Yellow and orange marks cover the crown, while teal, lavender and magenta lines surround the head and cross its outline.
records.reading: The three eye-like forms offer different ways into the face: a small diamond high on the forehead, a broad oval and a tightly ringed lower eye. Their uneven placement can read as startled or unsteady. Vertical bars across the mouth make the expression harder to settle. Warm yellows and oranges gather above while cool teal surrounds the head, keeping that unsettled gaze in a bright field.

records.title: Scrimshaw8
observations: A small elongated face and long neck sit within a wide spread of hair-like lines.
Black, pink and turquoise lines cross a bright yellow ground.
An oval on the forehead sits above the usual pair of eyes.
records.reading: A small elongated face sits within a much wider spread of black, pink and turquoise strands. The long neck draws attention downward, while a forehead oval and ordinary eye pair pull it back upward. Bright yellow remains visible through the open crossings. The contrast between the narrow head and its expansive surroundings gives this portrait a different scale at each stage of looking.

records.title: Scrimshaw15
observations: A face-like form fills the center, built from overlapping loops for eyes and a wide purple-pink mouth with black vertical tooth marks scratched inside.
Long streaks of red, yellow, orange, and blue radiate outward from the head, crossing over a bright blue background visible at the corners and edges.
A pale yellow-green wash fills the interior of the face, while surrounding lines alternate between thick opaque strokes and thin scratchy marks.
records.reading: The face seems to buckle under its own tangled lines—eyes built as lopsided concentric loops that sink at different heights, a mouth stretched wide with jagged marks scratched into purple. Radiating hair-like strokes push outward in every direction, giving the head a sense of unraveling. Against the cool blue ground, the warm yellows and reds inside read as feverish, suggesting a scream caught mid-breath.

records.title: Stick Together
observations: Five upright figures stand side by side across the image.
Long colored regions distinguish their bodies while thin lines cross the boundaries.
Looped white and yellow marks hover above the heads.
records.reading: Five upright figures stand close together, their long colored bodies filling the square. Thin lines cross between them, while differences in facial marks and color keep each figure distinct. Loops above their heads repeat the same gesture across the group. The title invites a reading of solidarity; the uneven faces and tangled boundaries keep that togetherness from feeling uniform.

records.title: Scrimshaw14
observations: A large face-like form fills the canvas, built from overlapping loops of blue, cyan, red, and black lines against a flat saturated yellow background.
Two asymmetric eye-like spirals dominate the upper half—the left layered in blue and gold rings, the right tighter with a black-and-white bullseye ringed in red and blue.
An open mouth shape at center-bottom shows jagged white teeth bordered by red, with a small red-rimmed circle floating below the chin area.
records.reading: The face stares outward through mismatched spiral eyes, one loose and layered, the other locked into a tight ring. Zigzag lines across the forehead and cheeks read as crackling tension, while the gaping mouth with its row of pointed teeth suggests a scream caught mid-breath. The bright yellow field pushes the tangled head forward, making the distress feel immediate rather than distant.

records.title: Scrimshaw2
observations: Concentric oval loops in blue, teal, and yellow fill the upper-left quadrant, forming two nested hollow shapes of unequal size.
A rounded rectangular region in the lower center contains dark purple zigzag marks bordered by teal and green lines, sitting inside a blue outline.
Vertical and wavy lines in pale blue, teal, and white run down both sides, layering over a saturated blue field and partially obscuring the central forms.
records.reading: A skull-like arrangement surfaces from dense, overlapping loops—two mismatched hollow shapes peer out from tangled blue and teal. The zigzag marks below read as both grin and grimace, lending the face an unsettled duality. Pale vertical lines drape across the surface like rain or static, partially dissolving the form back into pattern. The mood hovers between confrontation and cartoon humor.

records.title: Scrimshaw6
observations: A tilted warm-colored head appears against bright yellow.
Blue loops outline uneven eyes, a long nose and hair-like strands.
Broad translucent orange, pink and brown areas overlap within the face.
records.reading: A tilted head emerges from broad orange, pink and brown areas against bright yellow. Fine blue loops describe uneven eyes and a long nose, then extend into loose hair-like strands. The warmer masses give the face volume, while the blue lines keep its boundaries unsettled. Its open, irregular features can invite curiosity without resolving into a clearly named emotion.

records.title: Scrimshaw4
observations: A large rounded head shape dominates the center, built from overlapping dark purple, white, and cyan arcs against a flat sky-blue background.
Two eye forms sit asymmetrically: the left one wider with white and red marks inside, the right one tighter with concentric purple rings and a small red center.
A rectangular mouth area near the bottom shows jagged white zigzag teeth bordered by red lines, with a second smaller tooth-row visible below it.
records.reading: The face floats against open blue like something surfacing. Dense purple scribble builds the head's mass, while thin red and cyan lines escape outward, loosening the boundary between figure and field. The doubled mouth reads as uneasy—grinning and grimacing at once. Fewer layers and more bare ground leave the head exposed, as if it arrived before its surroundings could fill in.

records.title: Scrimshaw7
observations: A pink-lavender spiral sits upper-left on the head, with radiating dark, red, and gray lines fanning outward across the full width of the image.
Two large oval eye shapes contain concentric rings of green, purple, and white, flanking a vertical teal stripe running down the center of the face.
A tooth-filled mouth at the bottom shows jagged white triangular teeth between red lips, with scattered angular purple and pink marks filling the surrounding background.
records.reading: The face stares out through layered rings of color, its spiral crown pulling the eye upward while bared teeth anchor the composition below. The teal stripe splits the image into halves that don't quite mirror each other—one eye wider, one more buried in overlapping lines. The effect reads as alarm or confrontation, a face caught mid-shout against clashing yellows, pinks, and blues.

records.title: Scrimshaw5
observations: A skull-like head fills the frame, built from overlapping loops of red, purple, blue, and orange lines set against a saturated yellow background.
The left eye contains concentric rings with a cross-like mark in white and blue; the right eye is a tight black spiral ringed in red and brown.
A row of pointed teeth spans the lower face, and loose chain-like blue-gray loops run across the bottom above a blue and orange shape suggesting shoulders.
records.reading: Layered line loops construct a head that reads as both face and skull—exposed teeth grin below mismatched eyes, one marked with a symbol, the other a dark vortex. The hot yellow field pushes tangled reds and greens forward, producing a feeling of loud, unresolved tension. Chain-like forms at the bottom could suggest restraint or ornament, leaving the figure's mood open.

records.title: Scrimshaw 42
observations: A large skull-like form fills the frame in profile, built from overlapping loops of pink, yellow, cyan, and red lines against a solid black ground.
A jagged yellow crown shape sits at the upper right, its five pointed peaks drawn in a continuous stroke, resting near the top of the head.
Two spiral-centered eye forms appear at different depths—one purple with a white spiral core at center-left, one cyan loop to the right—while yellow horizontal bars suggest bared teeth at the bottom.
records.reading: Layered neon outlines trace and retrace a skull seen from the side, each color pass slightly offset so the form appears to vibrate against the black field. The crown reads less as decoration than as another restless loop, no more stable than the skull beneath it. A grinning unease comes through the bared-teeth bars and the mismatched, staring eye spirals, which refuse to settle into a single expression.

records.title: Scrimshaw 24
observations: A face-like form fills the center, built from tangled loops of purple, yellow, red, and teal lines over a mint-green interior and a lavender-purple background.
The left eye area contains a white X crossing inside a circular scribble, while the right eye is a looser spiral of yellow and blue lines with no blocking mark.
A wide mouth shape at the bottom shows vertical white bars resembling teeth, framed by red and dark blue overlapping strokes.
records.reading: The face emerges from accumulation—loops pile on loops until two asymmetric eye hollows and a barred mouth surface from the tangle. The white X over the left eye reads as sealed or struck through, giving the two sides different weight, as if one half watches and the other refuses. Purple scribbles spill past the face into the background, dissolving any boundary between figure and field. The effect can feel both frantic and oddly contained.

records.title: Trio1
observations: Three narrow upright figures stand on a warm orange field.
Red, blue, white and yellow lines form angular bodies and oval heads.
Radiating side marks and a larger oval above the middle figure interrupt the vertical grouping.
records.reading: Three narrow figures stand together in a field of orange, their upright bodies assembled from red, blue, white and yellow lines. Radiating marks extend sideways from the outer figures, while a larger oval hovers above the central one. These crossings give the group a shared structure without merging it into a single body. Looking can alternate between three characters and one interwoven pattern.

records.title: Scrimshaw12
observations: A roughly four-by-four grid of rounded rectangular shapes fills the canvas, each containing a simplified face with looping eyes, noses, and mouths drawn in heavy black lines.
A saturated purple-violet field dominates the background, interrupted by streaks of orange, yellow, white, and pink that cross over and between the face compartments.
Faces vary in fill color—muted green, peach, lavender, gray—giving each cell a distinct tonal identity despite the uniform black outlines binding them together.
records.reading: The grid reads like a crowd pressed together, each face boxed in yet bleeding into its neighbors through tangled overlapping lines. Some mouths gape with visible teeth; others flatten into thin curves. The purple ground pushes the warmer fills forward, creating a sense of faces surfacing from noise. The effect can feel claustrophobic or communal depending on where the eye rests—every cell competes for attention, none fully wins.

records.title: Scrimshaw3
observations: Three rounded forms outlined in thick black strokes sit side by side, with looping lines suggesting circular eyes, ears, and tooth-filled mouths across the lower half.
A dense underlayer of orange, teal, blue, red, and pink scratchy lines fills the background, visible through and around the black outlines like a tangled web.
Bold white scrawled marks cut across the middle zone, overlapping the black forms and creating a loose scribble layer that partially obscures the shapes beneath.
records.reading: Three black-outlined heads crowd the frame shoulder to shoulder, their features reduced to loops and open curves. Behind them, a hot orange-and-purple field of tangled lines pulses through every gap. The white scrawl layered across their faces reads as interruption—obscuring mouths and eyes, lending the group a feeling of being spoken over or half-erased. The composition can feel both communal and chaotic, figures jostling for visibility.

records.title: GM
observations: Two large letterforms—a rounded 'G' and an angular 'M'—fill the composition, built from overlapping strokes in blue, cyan, yellow, magenta, and white.
The 'G' contains concentric curved loops at its center with a nested rectangular shape filled by warm yellow and pink scribbles, forming a dense focal knot.
A loose border of yellow and white scrawled lines frames the edges, while flat muted blocks—olive, dark purple, ochre—sit behind the tangled linework.
records.reading: The two letters fill nearly the entire surface, yet they read less as text and more as scaffolding for layered color. Warm yellows and cool cyans compete across the strokes, giving the image a flickering, almost neon quality. The inner loops of the 'G' pull the eye inward, while the 'M' splays outward. The result can feel both greeting and shout—familiar letters made strange by sheer density of mark-making.

records.title: Scrimshaw9
observations: A head shape built from overlapping purple and dark blue contour lines sits against a flat salmon-pink background, tilted slightly left.
Bright cyan, yellow, green, and white strokes fill and surround the head, with a tight spiral of blue and orange lines forming a vortex at center-left.
Loose diagonal hatching in pink and white crosses the background at upper-left and lower-right, bleeding into the figure's edges and dissolving its boundary.
records.reading: The head emerges less as a solid form than as a collision of colored scribbles competing for the same space. A spiral near the center reads as an eye socket, pulling attention inward, while slashing cyan and white lines at the crown scatter it outward. The salmon field, warm and unbroken at the edges, makes the tangled interior feel pressurized—lines pushing against a soft, quiet container. The mood can feel frantic or playful depending on where you focus.

plan.introduction: These twenty-six works share a recurring subject—the face—yet treat it as a problem rather than a given. Lines crowd, cancel, and multiply features; grids press faces together; letters replace heads; groups of figures complicate the single portrait. Moving through the exhibition, a visitor can ask how much a face can absorb before it stops being a face, and what remains when the answer is unclear.

galleries.title: The Face as Field: Mark, Crowd, and Sign
galleries.question: How much pressure can a face absorb before it becomes something else entirely?
galleries.thesis: The exhibition opens with single heads built from competing marks, moves through asymmetry and doubling, widens into crowds and grids, and closes with two works—a five-letter greeting and a group of five figures—that replace or multiply the face, asking whether the subject was ever singular to begin with.
